title: Sequence-aware calibration + traffic mirroring and automated precision-degrade policy
creator: Anita Chopra
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable calibration pipeline that is sequence-length aware, enable non-invasive traffic mirroring for canary evaluation of FP8/INT8 profiles, and implement an automated degrade-to-float fallback policy when quality gates fail. Motivation: we want to safely roll out aggressive quantized profiles for cost savings while ensuring regressions are caught early and traffic is diverted without user-visible errors. This ticket contains design decisions, implementation plan, observability requirements, and rollback/fallback automation requirements.

Scope:
- Calibration service that produces quantization profiles binned by sequence-length and request shape (batch sizes, presence of long prompts).
- Traffic mirroring proxy to send a configurable % of live requests to the quantized variant (no live response returned to user) and record side-by-side outputs for comparison.
- Canary gating logic in the routing layer to automatically switch traffic to float32 variant for affected routes/customers when metrics exceed thresholds.
- Dashboard and alerting for quality regressions (embedding cosine similarity, generation token-level perplexity delta, and end-to-end task metrics where available).
- Integration with rollout manager to support staged increases and automated pause/rollback.

Key design notes / trade-offs considered:
1) Sequence-aware calibration: calibration uses stratified bins (short: <=64, medium: 65-512, long: >512 tokens) and collects activation distributions per-layer per-bin. This increases calibration time and storage but yields much higher fidelity profiles compared to a global calibration; chosen because we saw larger error variance for long-context prompts in recent evals.
2) Mirroring vs shadowing: we implement non-blocking mirroring (no extra latency on main path) and a lightweight batching path for quantized execution to approximate production latency. We accept some divergence in latency metrics for the mirrored runs but will calibrate a latency-correction factor in dashboards.
3) Metric selection: primary quality signals are embedding cosine similarity (for retrieval/semantic tasks), token-level KL/perplexity relative to baseline, and a task-level accuracy suite (where labeled golden answers exist). Embedding cosine similarity threshold default = 0.985 over a rolling 60-minute window for P0 routes; for P1 routes threshold = 0.98.
4) Fallback policy: automated degrade-to-float (route failing requests to float32 variant) is preferred over immediate rollback of the model rollout because it minimizes user impact and keeps rollout cadence. Full rollback of the model binary is still supported as a secondary action.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (calibration harness, offline):
- Build per-seq-length activation collector integrated into existing calib harness (ENG-68910 dependency).
- Produce profile artifacts tagged by bin and model-version. Store in artifact store with metadata.
- Offline evaluation runner that computes metrics vs float baseline for standard eval sets and customer prompt snapshots.
Phase 2 (mirroring infra & telemetry):
- Implement Mirroring proxy (configurable percent, per-route, and per-customer flags). Mirrored requests go to quantized path and are stored in the eval queue.
- Light-weight mirrored executor using smaller batch windows to avoid inflating production latency.
- Telemetry ingestion pipeline for side-by-side outputs and metrics (embedding similarity, perplexity, token delta).
Phase 3 (gating & automated fallback):
- Canary gating service that consumes telemetry and applies rolling-window rules.
- Automated degrade-to-float policy in routing layer: on trigger, route matched traffic to float variant and annotate events to rollout manager for operator review.
- Backoff and retry logic: if the quantized profile recovers (metrics return to acceptable range for 30 minutes), allow staged resume at reduced traffic share.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration pipeline can produce and retrieve per-bin profile artifacts for an input model and sequence-length distribution.
- Mirroring proxy can attach to existing routes and mirror 1-20% of live traffic without adding >5ms p99 latency to main path (measured over 1 hour).
- Telemetry pipeline shows side-by-side metrics and computes rolling-window regressions; alert fires when thresholds exceeded.
- On threshold breach, routing layer automatically degrades affected traffic to float variant within 60 seconds and creates an incident in the rollout manager.
- Manual rollback/reinstate through Console UI and API is possible.

Acceptance test plan:
- Synthetic prompts across bins and golden test suite run offline to validate metric calculations.
- Canary runs in staging with 5% mirroring for two weeks using replayed production snapshots.
- Small public canary on low-risk customer segment (feature-flagged) with mirroring+metrics visible to SRE/PM; confirm degrade-to-float triggers correctly via injected regression tests.

Observability & dashboards:
- New dashboard: "Quant Canary — Profile X" showing: traffic share, embedding similarity histogram, token-level KL heatmap by layer, latency impact for mirrored runs, and rolling percent of requests auto-degraded.
- Alerting: severity P0 (pager) for >2% absolute drop in embedding similarity over 10 minutes for high-tier routes; P1 email for smaller deltas.

Security & compliance:
- Mirrored requests contain request metadata and partial outputs — must not include raw customer PII in logs. Coordinate with Security (see security_review_required=true). Use KMS for profile artifacts.

Risks & mitigations:
- Cost: mirrored inference increases compute cost. Mitigate with low-percent mirroring, sampling, and time-limited canaries.
- False positives: metric tuning required to avoid noisy fallbacks; will use label smoothing and multiple metrics before triggering automated degrade.
- Latency divergence: mirrored path not identical to production; latency-correction factor and explicit latency metrics will be surfaced.

Deliverables:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7896 (calibration collection)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/2141 (mirroring proxy)
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/842239/Sequence+Aware+Calibration+and+Mirroring
- Dashboard: /console/dashboards/quant_canary_profile_x

Next steps this week:
- (Anita) finalize calibration bin boundaries and sample requirements (num prompts per bin).
- (Marco) prototype mirror execution path with a 1% sample and report p50/p95 latency delta.
- (SRE) advise on safe rollout limits and budgeting for mirroring costs.
